note: THE ONE VECTOR SET of the picture's reference cell (media lane A; media.md item 4 and section Open, ONE STRICTNESS AT THREE PARSERS; PATTERNS P5): every parser of the cell -- skepd's media/cell.rs, the shell's, the browser page's -- runs these in its own gate. The rule is the arbiter: parse(b) answers a cell only where b == encode(parse(b)). `verdict` is `cell` (admitted: the body IS the canonical form) or `no_cell`; `names_kind` says whether the body's `type` member names the cell's kind, which is what a reader whose null permits a permanent act halts on (DOCTRINE D13's carve-out) -- the daemon's write door refuses such a value by name (unknown_cell_schema) and treats a value not naming the kind as ordinary. A body carried as `body_hex` is bytes that are no UTF-8 string. Each pin here is INTERIM (the board's sm-Q8), confirmed at the media round.

vectors.name: canonical
vectors.why: the one form: type, hash, size in that order, no whitespace, lowercase hex

vectors.name: canonical_size_zero
vectors.why: a byte count of zero is a count; the schema judges form, lane B judges the file

vectors.name: canonical_size_max
vectors.why: 2^53 - 1, the largest count every JavaScript-backed reader reads exactly

vectors.name: two_hash_members
vectors.why: the two-hash body: a parser could bind one and a reader check the other; refused by the canonical rule at every parser

vectors.name: size_as_string
vectors.why: size is a JSON number, never a string

vectors.name: extent_member
vectors.why: the v1 cell carries no extent member (ms5-D2): a video-era member is a second schema

vectors.name: member_order
vectors.why: the members in any other order round-trip to different bytes

vectors.name: uppercase_hex
vectors.why: the hash is 64 LOWERCASE hex characters; uppercase re-encodes lowercase and fails the compare

vectors.name: hex_63
vectors.why: 63 hex characters are no 32-byte hash

vectors.name: hex_65
vectors.why: 65 hex characters are no 32-byte hash

vectors.name: hex_not_hex
vectors.why: a non-hex character in the hash

vectors.name: second_designation
vectors.why: H1: a value naming the kind under a second schema's form parses under no pinned schema; the daemon halts on it, never admits it as absent

vectors.name: whitespace
vectors.why: parses to the same cell and re-encodes to different bytes: b != encode(parse(b))

vectors.name: trailing_newline
vectors.why: a trailing byte: JSON admits it, the canonical rule does not

vectors.name: size_fraction
vectors.why: size is an integer

vectors.name: size_negative
vectors.why: size is non-negative

vectors.name: size_past_2_53
vectors.why: 2^53: a count a JavaScript-backed reader cannot read exactly

vectors.name: missing_size
vectors.why: the arity is closed: three members, each present

vectors.name: missing_hash
vectors.why: the arity is closed: three members, each present

vectors.name: hash_not_a_string
vectors.why: hash is a string

vectors.name: fourth_member
vectors.why: the arity is closed: a fourth member of any name is a second schema

vectors.name: another_kind
vectors.why: a type naming another kind (the enrollment record's) is not the cell's; its own schema reads it

vectors.name: type_not_a_string
vectors.why: a type that is no string names no kind

vectors.name: no_type
vectors.why: no type member names no kind (D13: every record body names its type)

vectors.name: prose
vectors.why: prose is no JSON object

vectors.name: pr_enc_def
vectors.why: a predicate def's PR-ENC envelope (a varint length, then bytes, 0xff among them: no UTF-8 string) is no JSON object

vectors.name: not_json
vectors.why: not JSON at all (unterminated): every schema is JSON, so nothing names the kind here

vectors.name: size_leading_zero
vectors.why: not JSON at all (a leading zero): a standard JSON parser reads no value, so nothing names the kind

vectors.name: empty_object
vectors.why: an object naming no type

vectors.name: json_array
vectors.why: a cell inside an array is no cell: the value is one object

vectors.name: past_the_cap
vectors.why: a body past the cell's cap (1024 bytes) is parsed by no reader of a cell, so it names nothing; a canonical cell is under 140 bytes
